text: The gauge choice ∇·A = 0, in which the scalar potential is fixed instantaneously by the charge distribution through Poisson's equation, is called the ___ gauge.
explanation: The condition ∇·A = 0 defines the Coulomb (or radiation) gauge; in it Gauss's law becomes ∇²φ = −ρ/ε₀, so φ responds instantaneously to ρ while A carries the radiation degrees of freedom. It is the non-covariant counterpart of the Lorenz gauge ∂_μ A^μ = 0.
